Federated Learning (FL) helps preserve privacy by keeping raw data on local devices, but integrating blockchain-based accountability into FL can introduce prohibitive storage, latency, and gas overhead when model updates are recorded on-chain. This paper introduces ReMerkle, a lightweight blockchain-enabled FL framework for consumer IoMT. ReMerkle combines a three-tier reputation mechanism based on cosine similarity, Beta-history reputation, and entropy-based quality assessment to filter unreliable or low-quality updates before aggregation. To reduce blockchain overhead, ReMerkle stores only a 32-byte Merkle root on-chain through Compact Merkle Tree Verification rather than storing full model updates. Experiments on a WBAN human activity recognition dataset show that ReMerkle achieves 90.2% accuracy after 10 FL rounds, increases honest-node reputation scores from 0.5 to 0.85, and requires 20,180 gas per five-client round, reducing both gas consumption and on-chain storage by 99.96% relative to full-update storage. These results demonstrate a cost-efficient and auditable FL architecture for secure consumer health monitoring.
10.1109/taffc.2026.3723127: Micro-expressions (MEs) are spontaneous, subtle facial movements that reveal genuine emotions, making them indispensable for high-stakes applications like security and clinical diagnosis. However, Micro-Expression Recognition (MER) is currently hindered by a dual bottleneck: the intrinsic difficulty of extracting discriminative features from subtle motions and the extrinsic privacy constraints that restrict centralized training in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose FED-PsyAU, a unified framework that synergizes psychological insights with privacy-preserving computing. First, addressing the feature representation challenge, we propose a psychological study, which quantifies the coordination and incoordination between upper and lower facial Action Units (AUs). Leveraging these priors, we develop a Dynamic Prior Knowledge-based Graph Attention Network (DPK-GAT) combined with a novel Spatial Position-Aware Transformer (SPAT) and an Expression-Specific Attention (ESA) module. This architecture effectively integrates structural psychological constraints with data-driven statistical patterns to learn hierarchical facial motion features. Furthermore, to tackle data privacy and scarcity, we integrate this model into a Personalized Federated Learning (P-FedProx) framework, enabling collaborative training across distributed clients without raw data exchange. Extensive experiments on standard ME databases demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both centralized and federated settings, validating the efficacy of incorporating psychological topology into privacy-preserving systems. Our implementation is publicly available athttps://github.com/MELABIPCAS/FED-PsyAU.git.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3722832: Federated learning (FL) applications normally employ large deep learning (DL) models, resulting in excessive communication overhead in the deployment of FL over resource-constraint mobile edge networks. To achieve better scalability for DL-based FL, we capitalize on both the asymmetric nature of mobile networks and the distinct effects of partial transmissions on FL training for the global and local models. We proposeFed-DynAmal, an FL framework that decreases the number of parameters transmitted in the uplink (clients-to-server) while concurrently achieving better model performance. The underlying idea is that each selected client sends a partial DL model to the server by omitting several sub-blocks from the trained local model. Crucially, we drop the assumption that transmitted local models can still be used for inference, thereby allowing for greater model variability. At the server, we introduce amalgamation, a process to merge different partial local models into an inference-viable full model. Essentially, amalgamation is a bridge for performing aggregation at the sub-block level. Interestingly, as the key takeaway, communication efficiency versus model performance is not necessarily a trade-off in FL: Our extensive experiments show thatFed-DynAmalcan effectively improve communication efficiency while still concurrently achieving higher accuracy and enhanced robustness.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3722528: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized devices without sharing private data. To address the performance degradation caused by statistical heterogeneity (non-IID data), Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) has emerged as a promising paradigm by tailoring models to individual clients. However, the decentralized and heterogeneous nature of PFL makes it highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where clients employ diverse architectures and the server cannot directly inspect or compare local model updates. Consequently, traditional defenses based on parameter aggregation or anomaly detection become ineffective. To tackle this challenge, we propose PIRD-PFL (Purifying Injection and Robust Distillation in PFL), a novel model that secures knowledge transfer in heterogeneous PFL without relying on parameter alignment or clean proxy data. The key idea is to purify malicious knowledge at both the sample and feature levels during the collaborative learning process. Specifically, PIRD-PFL consists of two synergistic phases. In the Injection Phase, we design a Channel Shuffling Vaccine (SV) mechanism that identifies and suppresses poisoned samples by exploiting their unstable responses under deep-layer channel perturbations. In the Distillation Phase, we develop a Robust Transmitter with Heterogeneous Attention Transfer (HAT) to enforce attention consistency on clean semantic regions, thereby preventing the propagation of malicious localized triggers. Extensive experiments on bench mark datasets demonstrate that PIRD-PFL effectively mitigates distributed backdoor attacks while maintaining high personalized accuracy, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art defenses in heterogeneous settings.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3722165: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) has emerged as a transformative server-free paradigm that enables collaborative learning over large-scale heterogeneous networks. However, it continues to face fundamental challenges, including data heterogeneity, restrictive assumptions for theoretical analysis, and degraded convergence when standard communication- or privacy-enhancing techniques are applied. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper develops a novel algorithm, PaME (DFL by Partial Message Exchange). The central principle is to allow only randomly selected sparse coordinates to be exchanged between two neighbor nodes. As a result, PaME significantly reduces communication costs while simultaneously limiting the exposure of data-sensitive information during transmission. The latter property is rigorously characterized by a formal reconstruction-risk theory under partial observation. Moreover, the algorithm is proven to converge in expectation to a stationary point at a linear rate, provided that the gradient is locally Lipschitz continuous and the communication matrix is doubly stochastic. These two mild assumptions not only dispenses with many restrictive conditions commonly imposed by existing DFL methods but also enables PaME to effectively address data heterogeneity. Furthermore, comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate its superior performance compared with several representative decentralized learning algorithms.
10.1109/tmm.2026.3722104: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed learning paradigm that collaboratively trains multiple client models to aggregate a generalized global model in server, without revealing data privacy. A key challenge to ideal global model aggregation is the problem of data heterogeneity. Despite many efforts to solve this problem in image data, there is still further exploration needed in skeletal data. Unlike image data, skeletal data is sparser, prompting the Skeleton Recognition Task (SRT) to prioritize fine-grained discrimination of part-body actions. In FL scenario, SRT demands a precise balance between commonalities and differences in local and global model parameters. In this paper, we propose a novel Federated Self-Supervised Skeletal Action Recognition framework (FedIGA). With the mission of mitigating data heterogeneity for improving global model aggregation, two key points are raised. Specifically, Projector-Specialty Regularization (PSR) is presented to indirectly elevate encoder training by deriving the intrinsic specialty of the projector, besides the direct regularization of the encoder. Furthermore, considering the main homogeneity and a few heterogeneity in the global model aggregation, SVD-Divergence Aggregation (SDA) is introduced to leverage the aggregation weight obtained by SVD-Param divergence to reduce the divergence between the client and global model for aggregating, based on the principle of seeking common ground while reserving differences. Extensive experiments show that FedIGA outperforms other baselines significantly on the public datasets.
